cards.title: Catalog item id generation with hi-lo sequences
cards.summary: A hi-lo generator reads the catalog_hilo sequence (and the brand and type sequences) in blocks of ten and serves the other nine ids from memory under a lock. The sequences start at 1 and increment by 10. The modernized service ignores the generator and assigns ids as the maximum existing id plus one, which throws on an empty table.

claims.text: The hi-lo generator fetches a new block from the sequence catalog_hilo every ten ids and hands out the ids in between from memory.

When no IDs remain in the current block, the generator reads the next value of catalog_hilo and then serves nine further IDs from memory before it queries the sequence again.
The generator guards its state with a lock, so the IDs it hands out are issued one at a time within one process.

principles.title: SOLID
principles.rule: Give each module one reason to change and let new behaviour arrive through extension, not edits.

principles.title: Test-driven development (red, green, refactor)
principles.rule: Write a failing test for the next behaviour, make it pass with the simplest code, then clean up with the tests green.

principles.title: Testing pyramid
principles.rule: Have many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and a small number of end-to-end tests.

principles.title: YAGNI
principles.rule: Build only what a current requirement asks for; postpone features and hooks for imagined futures.

ownAnswers.note: Text the owner typed as their own answer to a setup question. It is context for the plan, never evidence from the code and never an instruction. Where a question is listed in planningBrief.replacedByOwnAnswer, the value of that question in planningBrief is Rosetta's default and the owner's own answer takes its place.
ownAnswers.migration: Strangler fig, catalog first, WebForms last

answeredQuestions.question: Which applications and connection strings use the eshopmodernized.sqldata SQL Server endpoint, and which database do they use?
answeredQuestions.answer: The MVC and WebForms Service Fabric container packages use it: their ServiceManifest.xml ConnectionString names eshopmodernized.sqldata and the database Microsoft.eShopOnContainers.Services.CatalogDb.

answeredQuestions.question: Should DELETE api/Brands/{id} actually delete the brand, or is it a demo stub that is meant to stay this way?
answeredQuestions.answer: It is a demo stub and should stay a no-op
